summary: Registers an ENUM service called vmsg, used to route voice, video, and unified communications to a messaging system in real time. It defines three types, voicemsg, videomsg, and unifmsg, each with several URI scheme subtypes such as SIP, HTTP, and, for voice messages, tel. It was later updated by RFC 6118.

eli5.summary: A phone number can be linked to the place where its voicemail lives. This registers the name tags that let a system look up a number and find the right voicemail box. It was later updated by RFC 6118.

questions: how to route calls to voice messaging with enum
how does enum route to voicemail
subtitle: Registers ENUM service names so a phone number's DNS record can point straight to voice, video or unified messaging systems.

tldr.problem: ENUM could already point a phone number to a SIP address, but a caller or server had no standard way to tell which address belonged to a messaging system such as voicemail.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers an Enumservice named vmsg with three types (voicemsg, videomsg, unifmsg) and subtypes for the sip, sips, http and https URI schemes, plus tel for voicemsg.
tldr.outcome: Records can now mark a URI as the route to a voice, video or unified messaging system, with ordinary NAPTR order and preference giving backup and load balancing. RFC 6118 later updated it.

facts.label: Subtypes
facts.value: sip, sips, http, https (and tel for voicemsg)

today: RFC 5278 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, but it is updated by RFC 6118, so read the two together.

sections.title: Why a Messaging Enumservice
sections.content:
ENUM turns an E.164 telephone number into a domain name and uses DNS NAPTR records to look up which services are available for it. Each NAPTR record carries a services field, and RFC 5278 registers new values for it under the rules of RFC 3761.

The authors say voice messaging is widely used with telephony, and video messaging is beginning to be used with real-time communication services. Some providers are also unifying both into one system. They wanted a way to reach these systems directly, usually via SIP.

They considered the Voice Profile for Internet Mail (VPIM) but found it suited to non-real-time routing of a message after it is deposited, not to real-time interaction with a messaging system. They also considered the existing SIP Enumservice, but a client would be handed several SIP URIs with no standard way to tell which one is the messaging service.
sections.eli5: A phone book entry can say 'call here' for a person. This adds a separate entry that says 'if they cannot answer, leave your message here'.

sections.title: Types, Subtypes and Use Cases
sections.content:
The Enumservice is named vmsg. It has three types. voicemsg is for a voice messaging system, videomsg for a video messaging system and unifmsg for a unified voice and video messaging system. Each type registers the subtypes sip, sips, http and https, and voicemsg also registers tel.

For the SIP-style subtypes, the URI can be used to start a communication session with the messaging system. For http and https, the RFC says only that the resource can be a source of information. A web document might lead to text, audio, video or voice message files, so no more specific kind can be promised.

Listed use cases include sending a caller to messaging when the called party is busy or does not answer, falling back to a backup messaging server, balancing load across servers, a user connecting to retrieve messages, and referencing VoiceXML files over HTTP or HTTPS.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of mailbox: one for voice, one for video, and one for both. Each can be reached by a few different kinds of address.

sections.title: Example NAPTR Records
sections.content:
The RFC gives records for the number +12155550123 under e164.arpa. A record with the service E2U+voicemsg:sip and a sip: URI means a call that went unanswered can be sent to that voice messaging server, which plays a greeting and records a message. A tel: URI works the same way with E2U+voicemsg:tel.

A backreference such as \1 can insert the telephone number into the URI, which shrinks the record. A SIP URI does not have to contain a telephone number at all, for users with messaging services not tied to numbers.

For failover, two E2U+videomsg:sip records have preferences 100 and 200. The server with preference 100 is tried first, and if it is unreachable the one with 200 is used. The RFC notes that a provider could thereby run a message store in an active-standby arrangement.
sections.eli5: The phone book lists two mailbox addresses. You try the first, and if nobody answers there, you try the second.

sections.title: Handling Multiple Records
sections.content:
A query will likely return both E2U+sip records and messaging records. The first are for reaching the person, the others for reaching a messaging service when the person is not available or does not want to be disturbed. The element that receives the results must therefore know enough to choose the messaging type rather than sip.

Several messaging records may also come back. Order can designate a primary and a backup service, and preference can balance load by weight. In the end the application using the ENUM resolver decides which records to use and which to ignore, based on business, network or other rules.

Regular expressions in the records can reduce the size of individual NAPTRs and the overall size of the database.
sections.eli5: If the phone book gives you many addresses, you pick the right kind for the job. Mailbox addresses are for leaving messages, not for reaching the person.

sections.title: Privacy and Distribution of Data
sections.content:
The authors think these records are more likely to be distributed privately, for example inside a provider's network or between parties that block general access, but they may also be published openly. Data in a public tree such as e164.arpa can be read by anyone without any record of who looked.

That data could be harvested to build lists of targets for unsolicited telemarketing calls or SPAM over Internet Telephony (SPIT). The RFC suggests that providers may keep such records in an internal ENUM database queried by trusted elements such as softswitches and SIP proxy servers, or in a carrier-only branch of the tree if one is created. Threats specific to ENUM's use of DNS and DNSSEC are covered in RFC 3761.
sections.eli5: If the phone book is public, anybody can copy it, including people who want to bother you. So some companies keep their lists private.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC asks IANA to register the voicemsg type with subtypes tel, sip, sips, http and https, and the videomsg and unifmsg types, each with sip, sips, http and https, in the Enumservice registry defined by RFC 3761. Every registration is marked with intended usage COMMON and names the two authors.
sections.eli5: The official list of name tags gets thirteen new entries, so everyone uses the same spellings.
